mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 1.5% compresses discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days in any economic regime due to reduced cost of capital.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in >55% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 1.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in unemployment rate exceeding 0.2 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in >55% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.2pp in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous 6-month increases in GDP growth (GDPC1) and decreases in inflation (CPIAUCSL) relative to 6-month averages signal optimal economic conditions, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases > 0.5% YoY and CPIAUCSL decreases > 0.2% YoY in 6 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in >55% of instances when GDPC1 increases >0.5% YoY and CPIAUCSL decreases >0.2% YoY in 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 5% YoY) trigger Federal Reserve rate hikes that increase discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days due to reduced equity valuation multiples.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in >55% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 5% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts (HOUST) above its 12-month average signals robust consumer demand for construction, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in >55% of instances when HOUST is above its 12-month average.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) below 95.0 (2017=100) combined with GDP growth (GDPC1) < 0.5% YoY signals manufacturing contraction, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 95.0 and GDPC1 growth rate < 0.5% YoY
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in >55% of instances when INDPRO < 95.0 and GDPC1 growth rate < 0.5% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous 3-month increases in payrolls (PAYEMS) > 0.5% and decreases in unemployment rate (UNRATE) > 0.1 percentage points signal labor market strength, boosting consumer spending and generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 0.5% and UNRATE decreases > 0.1pp in 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in >55% of instances when PAYEMS increases >0.5% and UNRATE decreases >0.1pp in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Weak industrial production (INDPRO < 95.0) with low GDP growth (GDPC1 growth rate < 0.5% YoY) triggers recessionary fears, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 95.0 and GDPC1 growth rate < 0.5% YoY
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in >55% of instances when INDPRO < 95.0 and GDPC1 growth rate < 0.5% YoY.
